cards.explanation: The answer is famine, friends. The text says that when Elisha returned to Gilgal, "…there was a famine in the land." Food was running short, and that's the setting for everything that happens around this pot. A famine and a big pot of stew. I think everybody was watching that pot.

The answer is False, friends. The text says he cut them into the pot "…though no one knew what they were." Wild gourds from a wild vine, and not one person could name them. That's a lot of trust to put into a stew.

The answer is "There is death in the pot," friends. They cried out, "There is death in the pot, O man of God!" Notice they called out to Elisha, the man of God, right away. They knew who to take the problem to, and that's a good habit for any of us. Then the text says they could not eat it.
The answer is False, friends. The text says, "And they could not eat it." Nobody pushed through it and nobody played hero. They had a problem and Elisha was right there to hear it.

The answer is flour, friends. Elisha said, "Get some flour." and he threw it into the pot. Then he said, "Pour it out for the people to eat." The text says "…there was nothing harmful in the pot." He didn't dump the stew, he went for the flour.

The answer is True, friends. The text says, "And there was nothing harmful in the pot." Elisha threw in the flour, told them to pour it out, and the stew was no longer a problem. The text doesn't explain how it happened, and I won't pretend to.

The answers are people and eat, friends. Elisha said, "Give it to the people to eat…" The man from Baal-shalishah brought the loaves, and twenty of them were headed for the people, not set aside for someone important. The bread was for eating, plain and simple. In a famine, that's the best use for a sack of loaves.

The answer is that there are a hundred men to feed, friends. The servant asked, "How am I to set twenty loaves before a hundred men?" He did the math and the math looked rough. I think I'd have asked the exact same question, probably with a worse face.

The answer is "They will eat and have some left over," friends. Elisha said, "for this is what the LORD says: ‘They will eat and have some left over.’…" Elisha gave the servant that word before anyone had taken a single bite. A hundred men, twenty loaves, and the LORD says there's more than enough.
